Three values are enough for this study: light left as mostly bare paper, mid as even light hatching, and dark as closer marks. lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A ball is lit from above and slightly from the left. Where do light, mid and dark belong if you may use only those three values?

FEEDBACK
Leave the upper-left lit side mostly blank, hatch the middle lightly, and place the darkest marks on the lower-right and the small cast shadow. Three values turn the outline into a form because the eye can see a clear change. If every part is equally dark, the ball stays flat.

WATCH FOR
Pressing hard over the whole form makes a drawing more realistic, so no paper should be left bare.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Shade a pear with only three pencil values. Add a tiny key labelled light, mid and dark, and keep the lit side mostly bare paper.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Hana uses blank paper, light hatching and dense lines as three values on a tin. The tin is lit from the left, so the left side stays almost the colour of the paper. The front is hatched lightly for the mid value, and the right side plus the small shadow underneath receive closer lines. She does not cover the whole tin in one grey.

TRY FIRST
A ball is lit from above and slightly from the left. Where do light, mid and dark belong if you may use only those three values?

FEEDBACK
Leave the upper-left lit side mostly blank, hatch the middle lightly, and place the darkest marks on the lower-right and the small cast shadow. Three values turn the outline into a form because the eye can see a clear change. If every part is equally dark, the ball stays flat.
teach_steps.explain:
Tone is how light or dark a pencil mark is on a simple form. Three values are enough for this study: light left as mostly bare paper, mid as even light hatching, and dark as closer marks. Put the light value on the side the lamp reaches, the mid value where the form turns, and the dark value on the far side and in the cast shadow.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
